lessons.title: What Is AI? (Really)
lessons.subtitle: Cut through the hype and understand what AI actually is — in plain English

cards.headline: AI isn't magic. It's a pattern-matching machine — and once you understand it, everything changes.
cards.body: Every day, people around you are using AI to write faster, think clearer, and earn more. Today you'll learn exactly what AI is, how it works, and why it matters for you personally.
cards.statLabel: people use AI tools every month

cards.headline: AI in one sentence
cards.body: An AI model is a computer program trained on billions of examples of human text, images, and data — so it can predict what comes next in a conversation, an image, or a task.
bullets: It doesn't "think" the way humans do — it finds patterns
The more it's trained, the better its predictions get
Modern AI (like ChatGPT or Claude) is trained on most of the internet

cards.headline: The three AIs you need to know
cards.body: There are hundreds of AI tools, but three dominate for everyday use. Think of them like smartphones — different brands, similar jobs.
bullets: 🔵 ChatGPT (OpenAI) — The most popular. Great for everything from emails to code
🟠 Claude (Anthropic) — The most accurate for long, complex tasks and reasoning
🟣 Gemini (Google) — Built into Google Workspace; great for search and documents

cards.headline: What AI is NOT
cards.body: Most people's fears about AI come from misunderstanding it. Let's clear that up right now.
bullets: ❌ It's not conscious — it has no feelings, opinions, or desires
❌ It's not always right — it can confidently state wrong facts (we'll cover this)
❌ It's not going to take every job — but people using AI will outcompete those who don't
✅ It IS a powerful tool — like a calculator for your brain

cards.headline: Your task today
cards.body: Open ChatGPT (chat.openai.com) or Claude (claude.ai) — both are free. Type this exact prompt and see what happens:
bullets: "Explain to me in 3 bullet points what you are and what you're good at."
Notice how it answers in a natural, conversational way
That response comes from pattern-matching on millions of similar questions

quiz.question: At its core, how does an AI model like ChatGPT work?
options: It searches the internet in real time to find answers
It predicts likely responses based on patterns learned from training data
It connects to a team of human experts who type the replies
It uses a pre-written database of questions and answers
quiz.explanation: AI models like ChatGPT are trained on vast amounts of text and learn to predict what a helpful, relevant response looks like. They don't search the internet in real time (though some have add-on tools that do) — the knowledge is baked in from training.

quiz.question: Which AI tool is most commonly described as the best choice for long, complex reasoning tasks?
options: ChatGPT
Gemini
Claude
Copilot
quiz.explanation: Claude (made by Anthropic) is widely recognised for its accuracy and strength at long-form, complex reasoning and writing tasks. ChatGPT is the most popular overall, while Gemini is deeply integrated into Google's tools.

quiz.question: AI is conscious and has real opinions about the answers it gives.
options: True
False
quiz.explanation: False. AI models have no consciousness, feelings, or opinions. They generate responses based on statistical patterns — not beliefs or desires. When an AI sounds confident, that's the pattern of human confident writing, not genuine certainty.

quiz.question: Which of these is the BEST way to think about what an AI tool is?
options: A replacement for human intelligence
A magic box that always knows the right answer
A powerful calculator for language and thinking tasks
A search engine with better design
quiz.explanation: Thinking of AI as a "calculator for your brain" is the most useful mental model. Just like a calculator doesn't replace understanding maths, AI doesn't replace your thinking — but it dramatically speeds up and amplifies what you can do.

lessons.title: Meet Your AI Toolkit
lessons.subtitle: A hands-on tour of the three tools you'll use every day — and when to reach for each one

cards.headline: A carpenter doesn't use a hammer for everything. Neither should you with AI.
cards.body: ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini each have different strengths. Knowing which to use — and when — is one of the most valuable skills you can build this month.
cards.statLabel: cover 95% of everything you'll ever need AI for

cards.headline: ChatGPT — the Swiss Army knife
cards.body: Made by OpenAI, ChatGPT is the most widely used AI in the world. It's versatile, fast, and has the largest ecosystem of plugins and integrations.
bullets: ✅ Best for: everyday tasks, brainstorming, coding, image generation (GPT-4o)
✅ Best for: searching the web in real time (with browsing enabled)
✅ Best for: using AI tools inside other apps (it's built into hundreds)
⚠️ Watch out: can sound confident even when wrong — always double-check facts

cards.headline: Claude — the deep thinker
cards.body: Made by Anthropic, Claude is built for accuracy, nuance, and long-form tasks. If you need to analyse a 50-page document or write something genuinely thoughtful, Claude is your go-to.
bullets: ✅ Best for: long documents, contracts, reports, research analysis
✅ Best for: writing that needs a natural, human tone
✅ Best for: complex reasoning and step-by-step problem solving
⚠️ Watch out: slightly slower than ChatGPT; free tier has usage limits

cards.headline: Gemini — the Google native
cards.body: Google's AI is built directly into Gmail, Docs, Sheets, and Search. If you live in Google Workspace, Gemini is already there waiting for you.
bullets: ✅ Best for: summarising emails and drafting replies in Gmail
✅ Best for: analysing data in Google Sheets
✅ Best for: Google Search with AI-powered answers
⚠️ Watch out: most powerful features require a Google One AI Premium subscription

cards.headline: Your task today
cards.body: Ask the same question to both ChatGPT and Claude and compare the responses. Try this prompt:
bullets: "Give me 5 creative ways I could use AI to save time at work this week."
Notice the difference in tone, depth, and style
Neither answer is "better" — they're different. That's the point.

quiz.question: You need to analyse a 40-page business report and write a detailed summary. Which AI tool is best suited for this?
options: ChatGPT — it's the most popular
Claude — it's built for long, complex documents
Gemini — it integrates with Google Drive
It doesn't matter — they all do the same thing
quiz.explanation: Claude excels at long-form analysis and reasoning. Its large context window and focus on accuracy make it the top choice for analysing lengthy documents. While ChatGPT and Gemini can also handle documents, Claude is specifically optimised for this kind of deep work.

quiz.question: Which AI is most deeply integrated into Google Workspace tools like Gmail and Sheets?
options: ChatGPT
Claude
Gemini
Copilot
quiz.explanation: Gemini is Google's AI and is natively integrated into Gmail, Docs, Sheets, and Search. It's the natural choice if your work already lives in Google Workspace.

quiz.question: All three AI tools (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini) are always 100% factually accurate.
options: True
False
quiz.explanation: False. All AI tools can "hallucinate" — confidently stating things that are incorrect. This is one of the most important things to understand about AI. Always verify important facts, especially for anything legal, medical, or financial.

quiz.question: What is the most practical approach to choosing which AI tool to use?
options: Always use the most expensive one
Pick one and use it exclusively — switching is confusing
Match the tool's strengths to the task at hand
Use whichever one your friends use
quiz.explanation: The smartest approach is to know the strengths of each tool and match them to your task. Use ChatGPT for everyday versatility, Claude for deep analysis and writing, and Gemini when you're working inside Google's ecosystem.

lessons.title: Your First Great Prompt
lessons.subtitle: The single skill that separates people who get amazing results from people who get mediocre ones

cards.headline: The quality of your output is almost entirely determined by the quality of your input.
cards.body: Most people type vague one-liners and get vague, generic responses. Today you'll learn a simple framework that transforms how AI responds to you — permanently.
cards.statLabel: better results from the same AI with a better prompt

cards.headline: Why most prompts fail
cards.body: Imagine asking a new employee to "write something about marketing." You'd get something useless. But ask them to "write a 200-word Instagram caption for our summer sale, targeting 25–35 year old women, using a fun and energetic tone" — and you'd get something great.
bullets: AI works exactly the same way — vague in, vague out
The AI isn't failing; your instructions are incomplete
Adding context and specifics is the single biggest upgrade you can make

cards.headline: The CRAFT framework
cards.body: Use this five-part checklist to build any prompt. You don't need all five every time — but the more you include, the better the result.
bullets: 🎭 Context — who you are and what situation you're in
🎯 Role — tell AI who to BE ("act as an expert copywriter")
📋 Action — exactly what you want it to DO
📐 Format — how you want the output (bullet list, email, table, etc.)
🎨 Tone — the feeling or style (professional, casual, concise, funny)

cards.headline: CRAFT in action
cards.body: Let's see the difference a structured prompt makes.
bullets: ❌ Weak prompt: "Write an email about our product launch"

✅ Strong prompt: "Act as a senior copywriter. Write a 150-word email announcing the launch of our new AI productivity app to existing customers. Use an excited but professional tone. Include a clear CTA at the end."
Same AI. Same tool. Completely different result.

cards.headline: Your task today
cards.body: Take something you actually need done this week and write a CRAFT prompt for it. Try this template:
bullets: "Act as [role]. I am [your context]. Write [what you need] in [format]. Use a [tone] tone."
Paste it into ChatGPT or Claude
Then try the weak version of the same prompt and compare

quiz.question: In the CRAFT framework, what does the "R" stand for?
options: Result — what outcome you want
Role — who you want the AI to act as
Request — the specific ask
Revision — asking the AI to improve its answer
quiz.explanation: R stands for Role. Telling the AI to "act as an expert [X]" fundamentally changes the tone, depth, and accuracy of its response. An AI acting as a senior financial advisor will answer very differently to the same question than an AI with no role assigned.

quiz.question: Which of these is a better-structured prompt?
options: "Tell me about social media"
"Write something for LinkedIn"
"Act as a LinkedIn growth expert. Write a 150-word post about the benefits of remote work for a professional audience. Use a conversational, inspiring tone."
"Do social media for me"
quiz.explanation: Option C applies the CRAFT framework — it assigns a role, specifies the platform, sets a length, defines the topic and audience, and gives a tone. The other options are too vague to generate a useful, targeted response.

quiz.question: You need to include all five parts of the CRAFT framework in every prompt.
options: True
False
quiz.explanation: False. CRAFT is a checklist, not a rigid formula. A simple task might only need Context and Action. The framework is a guide to help you think about what extra detail would improve the result — use as many parts as the task needs.

quiz.question: Why does specifying a "Format" in your prompt matter?
options: It makes the AI work faster
It ensures the output is structured the way you actually need to use it
It reduces the AI's chance of making factual errors
It isn't important — AI always chooses the best format automatically
quiz.explanation: Specifying the format (bullet list, email, numbered steps, table, etc.) means you get output you can use immediately — no reformatting needed. If you don't specify, AI will pick a default format that may not suit your purpose.

lessons.title: Prompt Engineering 101
lessons.subtitle: Advanced techniques that unlock a completely different level of AI performance

cards.headline: Yesterday you learned to drive. Today you're learning the motorway.
cards.body: The CRAFT framework gives you solid results. These techniques take you from good to exceptional — and some of them will completely change how you think about what AI can do.
cards.statLabel: of AI users know and use these techniques

cards.headline: Technique 1: Chain of Thought
cards.body: Adding "think step by step" to any prompt forces AI to reason through a problem rather than jump to an answer. It dramatically improves accuracy on anything analytical.
bullets: ❌ "What's the best pricing strategy for my SaaS product?"
✅ "Think step by step. What's the best pricing strategy for my SaaS product targeting SMEs?"
Use it for: maths, decisions, business strategy, planning, troubleshooting
Why it works: it mirrors how humans think through complex problems

cards.headline: Technique 2: Give it examples
cards.body: Show AI what "good" looks like before asking it to produce something. This is called few-shot prompting — and it's one of the most powerful techniques available.
bullets: Add "Here is an example of the style I want:" followed by a sample
The AI will match the tone, format, and style of your example
Use it for: brand voice, writing style, content formats, data extraction
💡 You can even paste in your own previous writing as the example

cards.headline: Technique 3: Iterate, don't restart
cards.body: Most people throw away a response they don't like and start again. Experts refine in the same conversation. AI remembers everything you've discussed — use that.
bullets: "Make it shorter and more punchy"
"Rewrite the opening — it's too formal"
"Give me three alternative versions of the second paragraph"
"Now convert this into a bullet-point list"
Each follow-up message builds on what came before — it's a collaboration

cards.headline: Technique 4: Assign stakes
cards.body: Telling AI why something matters — or what's riding on the output — tends to improve the quality of its response.
bullets: ✅ "This email is going to 10,000 subscribers — it needs to be exceptional"
✅ "I'm presenting this to the board of directors tomorrow morning"
✅ "This is for a client paying £5,000 — the quality needs to reflect that"
It sounds odd, but adding stakes consistently produces more careful, thorough outputs

cards.headline: Your task today
cards.body: Pick any prompt you've used this week and upgrade it using at least two of today's techniques. Start with Chain of Thought + an example:
bullets: Add "Think step by step" to the beginning
Add "Here is an example of the style I want: [paste example]"
Compare the output to your original — the difference will surprise you

quiz.question: What does adding "think step by step" to a prompt do?
options: Makes the AI respond more slowly but with better formatting
Forces the AI to reason through the problem sequentially, improving accuracy
Tells the AI to use numbered lists in its response
Activates a special reasoning mode only available on paid plans
quiz.explanation: "Think step by step" is a Chain of Thought technique that prompts AI to work through a problem logically rather than jump to a conclusion. It's especially effective for maths, analysis, and multi-step decisions — and it works on all AI tools, free or paid.

quiz.question: What is "few-shot prompting"?
options: Keeping your prompts very short to save tokens
Providing examples of the output style you want before asking AI to produce something
Using AI for a limited number of tasks per day
A technique that only works with GPT-4 and above
quiz.explanation: Few-shot prompting means giving AI one or more examples of what you want before making your request. This is one of the most reliable ways to get output that matches a specific tone, format, or style — particularly useful for brand voice or structured data extraction.

quiz.question: If you don't like an AI response, the best approach is to start a brand new conversation.
options: True
False
quiz.explanation: False. It's almost always better to iterate within the same conversation. AI retains context throughout a chat, so follow-up instructions like "make it shorter" or "rewrite the opening" are much more efficient than starting over. Think of it as a collaboration, not a vending machine.

quiz.question: You're asking AI to help write a critical pitch deck for a major investor meeting. Which technique from today would most improve the output quality?
options: Using a very short prompt to keep things simple
Assigning stakes — telling AI this is for a major investor meeting
Starting a new conversation for each slide
Using only true/false questions in your prompt
quiz.explanation: Assigning stakes — explaining the importance and context of the task — consistently produces more careful, thorough responses. Combined with Chain of Thought and providing examples of great pitch decks, you'd get a significantly higher-quality output.

quiz.question: Which combination of techniques would be most powerful for getting AI to write in your exact brand voice?
options: Chain of Thought only
Assigning stakes and iterating
Few-shot prompting (providing examples) + specifying tone in the CRAFT format
Keeping the prompt as short as possible
quiz.explanation: Combining few-shot prompting (showing AI examples of your existing writing) with a specific tone instruction in the CRAFT format is the most reliable way to get AI to match your brand voice. The examples show AI what your voice looks and feels like; the tone instruction reinforces it.

lessons.title: ChatGPT Deep Dive
lessons.subtitle: Unlock everything the world's most popular AI can actually do — most people only scratch the surface

cards.headline: Most people use ChatGPT like a Google search. That's like using a Ferrari to park outside the supermarket.
cards.body: ChatGPT is far more powerful than most people realise. Today you'll go beyond basic questions and discover the features that make it genuinely transformative.
cards.statLabel: weekly active users — yet most use less than 10% of its features

cards.headline: The ChatGPT interface: what everything does
cards.body: Before you go deeper, it's worth knowing what you're working with. ChatGPT has several modes and tools baked in.
bullets: 💬 Chat — the standard text conversation you already know
📎 File upload — paste in PDFs, spreadsheets, images for analysis
🌐 Browse — real-time web search for current information
🖼️ Image generation — create images using DALL·E (GPT-4o)
📊 Data analysis — upload a spreadsheet and ask it to find patterns
🔌 GPTs — custom AI assistants built for specific jobs

cards.headline: Custom Instructions: set it and forget it
cards.body: This is one of the most underused features. Custom Instructions let you tell ChatGPT about yourself once — and it applies that context to every single conversation automatically.
bullets: Go to Settings → Custom Instructions
Tell it who you are: "I'm a freelance designer running a small studio. I work with SME clients. I prefer direct, concise responses."
Tell it how to respond: "Always give me options rather than one answer. Never be verbose."
💡 Think of it as permanently briefing your AI assistant

cards.headline: GPTs: AI tools built for specific jobs
cards.body: The GPT Store has thousands of custom AI assistants — each pre-configured for a specific task. Instead of writing a complex prompt from scratch, you use a GPT that's already been optimised.
bullets: 📝 Writing GPTs — trained on specific styles (academic, copywriting, SEO)
💻 Coding GPTs — specialised for specific languages or frameworks
🎨 Design GPTs — help with briefs, moodboards, creative direction
📈 Business GPTs — pitch decks, financial models, market research
🔍 Find them: click "Explore GPTs" in the left sidebar

cards.headline: Your task today
cards.body: Set up your Custom Instructions — this five-minute task will improve every ChatGPT conversation you have from today onwards.
bullets: Open ChatGPT → click your profile icon → Settings → Custom Instructions
In the first box, describe yourself, your work, and your goals
In the second box, describe how you want ChatGPT to respond
Then start a new conversation and notice how differently it responds

quiz.question: What do ChatGPT's Custom Instructions allow you to do?
options: Change the visual theme of the ChatGPT interface
Set permanent context about yourself so ChatGPT applies it to every conversation
Give ChatGPT access to your email and calendar
Unlock the GPT-4 model for free
quiz.explanation: Custom Instructions let you tell ChatGPT who you are, what you do, and how you like to receive responses — once. From then on, every conversation automatically benefits from that context. It's one of the highest-value settings available and takes under five minutes to set up.

quiz.question: What is a "GPT" in the ChatGPT GPT Store?
options: A paid upgrade to access more powerful AI models
A custom AI assistant pre-configured for a specific task or industry
A plugin that connects ChatGPT to external websites
A saved conversation template
quiz.explanation: GPTs are custom versions of ChatGPT that have been configured with specific instructions, knowledge, and tools for a particular purpose — like SEO writing, coding, or legal research. Using a well-built GPT often produces better results than writing your own prompt from scratch.

quiz.question: ChatGPT can analyse data from an uploaded spreadsheet and identify patterns.
options: True
False
quiz.explanation: True. ChatGPT's data analysis feature (available with GPT-4o) lets you upload spreadsheets and ask questions about the data — spotting trends, creating summaries, generating charts, and more. It's a powerful alternative to manual data analysis for non-technical users.

quiz.question: You want to know today's top news stories. Which ChatGPT feature should you use?
options: Standard chat — it already knows current events
Browse — which gives ChatGPT real-time access to the web
Image generation — it can visualise news stories
Data analysis — for processing news articles
quiz.explanation: ChatGPT's standard knowledge has a training cutoff and doesn't include today's news. The Browse feature (when enabled) lets ChatGPT search the web in real time, making it suitable for current events, recent prices, live data, and anything that's changed since its training.

lessons.title: Claude: The Thinking Person's AI
lessons.subtitle: Why Claude beats ChatGPT for certain tasks — and how to get the most out of it

cards.headline: If ChatGPT is a fast-talking generalist, Claude is the quiet expert who never guesses.
cards.body: Claude (made by Anthropic) has a different personality and different strengths to ChatGPT. Learning when to switch to Claude is one of the highest-leverage AI habits you can build.
cards.statLabel: tokens of context — Claude can read and remember a full novel in one session

cards.headline: Where Claude genuinely outperforms ChatGPT
cards.body: Claude isn't trying to be ChatGPT. It's built around different principles — accuracy, honesty, and depth. That makes it the better choice in specific situations.
bullets: 📄 Long documents — contracts, reports, research papers (huge context window)
✍️ Nuanced writing — content that sounds genuinely human, not AI-generated
🧠 Complex reasoning — multi-step problems, strategic thinking, analysis
📊 Detailed summaries — it reads the whole thing, not just the beginning
⚖️ Honest uncertainty — Claude says "I'm not sure" rather than making things up

cards.headline: Projects: Claude's killer feature
cards.body: Claude's Projects feature lets you create persistent AI workspaces with memory, custom instructions, and uploaded documents — all saved between sessions.
bullets: Create a Project for each area of your life or work
Upload relevant documents (company info, brand guides, style notes)
Set custom instructions for that specific context
💡 Example: a "Content Creation" project with your brand voice guide uploaded — Claude writes in your style every time, without re-explaining

cards.headline: The honest truth: when to use each
cards.body: You don't have to pick one. The most effective AI users switch between tools based on the task.
bullets: 🔵 Use ChatGPT for: quick tasks, browsing the web, image generation, coding, GPT plugins
🟠 Use Claude for: anything long, anything where accuracy matters, important writing
🟣 Use Gemini for: tasks inside Google Workspace
💡 Pro tip: draft a first version in ChatGPT, then paste into Claude and ask it to "improve the quality and make it sound more human"

cards.headline: Your task today
cards.body: Open Claude (claude.ai — free tier is excellent) and set up your first Project.
bullets: Click "Projects" in the left sidebar → New Project
Name it something useful (e.g. "Work Tasks" or "Content Writing")
In Project Instructions, paste a short description of who you are and how you want Claude to respond
Start a conversation inside the Project and notice how it feels different to a blank chat

quiz.question: What makes Claude particularly well-suited for analysing long documents?
options: It reads faster than ChatGPT
It has a very large context window, allowing it to process hundreds of thousands of words in one session
It connects to cloud storage automatically
It uses a special document-reading mode
quiz.explanation: Claude has one of the largest context windows available in any consumer AI tool — up to 200,000 tokens (roughly 150,000 words). This means it can read, retain, and reason about an entire lengthy document in a single conversation, without losing information the way shorter-context models do.

quiz.question: What is Claude's "Projects" feature designed for?
options: Managing your to-do list and calendar
Creating persistent AI workspaces with saved instructions, memory, and uploaded documents
Collaborating with other Claude users in real time
Generating AI images for specific projects
quiz.explanation: Projects give you a persistent AI workspace where you can upload documents, set specific instructions, and have Claude remember context between sessions. It's particularly powerful for recurring tasks — like content writing or client work — where you'd otherwise re-explain the context every time.

quiz.question: Claude will always give you a confident answer, even if it doesn't know something for certain.
options: True
False
quiz.explanation: False. One of Claude's distinguishing qualities is that it's designed to acknowledge uncertainty rather than fabricate answers. When Claude doesn't know something or isn't confident, it tends to say so — making it more trustworthy for tasks where accuracy is important.

quiz.question: You've drafted a blog post in ChatGPT but the writing feels generic and AI-ish. What's the smartest next step?
options: Delete it and start from scratch
Publish it as-is — readers won't notice
Paste it into Claude and ask it to improve the quality and make it sound more human
Switch to Gemini and regenerate the whole post
quiz.explanation: Using both tools together is a power move. ChatGPT is great for generating a first draft quickly; Claude excels at refining tone, improving quality, and making writing sound genuinely human. Passing content between tools is a common workflow among advanced AI users.

lessons.title: Module 1 Checkpoint
lessons.subtitle: Consolidate everything from this week — and prove to yourself how much you've already learned

cards.headline: Six days ago you knew almost nothing about AI. Look how far you've come.
cards.body: Today is about consolidation, not new information. We're going to revisit the most important ideas from this week, apply them in a real task, and set you up perfectly for Module 2.
cards.statLabel: mastered in your first week

cards.headline: Week 1 in review: the big ideas
cards.body: Here are the seven things you now know that most people don't.
bullets: 1️⃣ AI is a pattern-matching machine — powerful, but not magic
2️⃣ ChatGPT (versatile), Claude (deep), Gemini (Google) each have a sweet spot
3️⃣ Vague prompts produce vague outputs — specificity is everything
4️⃣ CRAFT (Context, Role, Action, Format, Tone) structures every great prompt
5️⃣ Chain of Thought, examples, iteration, and stakes all supercharge results
6️⃣ ChatGPT Custom Instructions permanently personalise your experience
7️⃣ Claude Projects create persistent workspaces that remember your context

cards.headline: The most important mindset shift
cards.body: The single biggest difference between people who get great results from AI and those who don't isn't the tool — it's how they think about it.
bullets: ❌ Treating AI like a search engine: "What is the best CRM?"

✅ Treating AI like a brilliant collaborator: "I run a 5-person consultancy. We're choosing between HubSpot and Salesforce. Think step by step and help me build a comparison framework for our specific needs."
The more context you give, the more value you get
AI rewards people who think carefully about what they're asking

cards.headline: What's coming in Module 2
cards.body: Next week, you move from understanding AI to making it part of your daily workflow. Module 2 is called Productivity Power — and it's where things start getting genuinely life-changing.
bullets: 📧 Day 8: Write and respond to emails 10× faster
📝 Day 9: Never take meeting notes manually again
🔍 Day 10: Research anything in a fraction of the time
✍️ Day 11: First drafts of anything in minutes
📋 Day 12–14: Build your personal AI productivity stack
🎯 By Day 14 you'll have a system that saves you 2+ hours every day

cards.headline: Your checkpoint challenge
cards.body: This is your first real test. Use everything from this week to complete the following task — it's something you'll actually be able to use:
bullets: Build a personal AI cheat sheet in ChatGPT or Claude

Prompt: "Act as an AI productivity coach. I am [describe yourself]. Create a personalised one-page AI toolkit guide for me — which tools I should use, for what tasks, and 3 example prompts tailored to my work."
Save the output — you'll refer back to it throughout this challenge
That's a CRAFT prompt, Chain of Thought context, and practical output all in one

quiz.question: According to the CRAFT framework, which element tells the AI who to "be" for the task?
options: Context
Role
Action
Tone
quiz.explanation: Role (the R in CRAFT) tells the AI to adopt a specific persona or expertise — "act as a senior marketing strategist" or "act as a patient teacher." This shapes the depth, tone, and approach of the entire response.

quiz.question: Which AI tool would you choose to read and summarise a 100-page legal contract?
options: ChatGPT — most popular so must be best
Gemini — it's connected to Google Drive
Claude — large context window and strong accuracy for long documents
Any tool will perform equally well
quiz.explanation: Claude is the clear choice for long documents. Its large context window means it can process the entire document without losing information, and its focus on accuracy reduces the risk of it misrepresenting critical legal details.

quiz.question: The most effective AI users stick to one AI tool and master it completely.
options: True
False
quiz.explanation: False. The most effective AI users match the tool to the task. ChatGPT for quick versatile tasks, Claude for deep analysis and quality writing, Gemini for Google Workspace. Using the right tool for the right job consistently outperforms mastering only one.

quiz.question: What prompt technique involves telling AI "think step by step"?
options: Few-shot prompting
Chain of Thought
Assigning stakes
Format specification
quiz.explanation: Chain of Thought prompting uses phrases like "think step by step" to encourage AI to reason through a problem sequentially rather than jumping to a conclusion. It's especially effective for analysis, decisions, maths, and any multi-step problem.

quiz.question: You want ChatGPT to always know your job, your preferences, and your communication style without having to explain it every time. What should you set up?
options: A new GPT in the GPT Store
Custom Instructions in Settings
A Claude Project
A saved prompt template
quiz.explanation: Custom Instructions (Settings → Custom Instructions in ChatGPT) let you set permanent context that applies to every conversation automatically. It's one of the highest-value five-minute setup tasks for any regular ChatGPT user.

lessons.title: AI Email Assistant
lessons.subtitle: Write, reply to, and manage emails in a fraction of the time — without sacrificing quality

cards.headline: The average professional spends 28% of their working week on email. AI can cut that in half — starting today.
cards.body: Email is the single biggest time drain in most people's working lives. Today you'll build an AI email workflow that handles drafts, replies, and follow-ups faster than you ever thought possible.
cards.statLabel: of the working week lost to email — on average

cards.headline: The four email tasks AI handles brilliantly
cards.body: You don't need AI for every email. But for these four situations, it's a game-changer.
bullets: ✍️ Drafting from scratch — give AI bullet points, it writes the full email
↩️ Replying to complex messages — paste the email in, AI drafts the response
📏 Adjusting length and tone — "make this shorter", "make it more formal"
🔁 Follow-ups — AI writes polite, non-pushy follow-up sequences automatically

cards.headline: The email prompt that works every time
cards.body: This template works for almost any professional email. Memorise it or save it.
bullets: "Act as a professional business writer. Write an email to [recipient/role]."
"The purpose is: [your goal in one sentence]."
"Key points to cover: [bullet list of what to include]."
"Tone: [professional / warm / assertive / concise]."
"Length: [short (under 100 words) / medium / long]."
💡 The more context you give, the less editing you'll need to do

cards.headline: Handling difficult emails with AI
cards.body: This is where AI becomes genuinely valuable. Difficult emails — complaints, salary negotiations, awkward client conversations — are ones most people dread and procrastinate on.
bullets: Paste in the difficult email you received
Tell AI: "This is a [complaint / demand / difficult request]. Help me write a response that is [calm / firm / empathetic] and achieves [your goal]."
AI removes the emotional charge from the task — you get a clear-headed draft instantly
✅ Always review and personalise before sending — AI sets the foundation, you add the human touch

cards.headline: Your task today
cards.body: Find one email in your drafts or inbox that you've been putting off writing. Use AI to draft it now.
bullets: Paste the context (or the email you're replying to) into ChatGPT or Claude
Use the email prompt template from today's lesson
Review, tweak, and send
Track how long it took vs. your normal drafting time

quiz.question: What is the most effective way to use AI for writing a complex email reply?
options: Ask AI to write it with no context and edit heavily afterwards
Paste in the original email and give AI clear context about your goal and desired tone
Use AI only for short emails — long ones still need to be written manually
Let AI send the email automatically without reviewing it
quiz.explanation: Pasting in the original email gives AI the full context it needs to write a relevant, targeted reply. Adding your goal and tone means the draft will need minimal editing. Always review before sending — AI sets the foundation, but your judgment and personal touch are what make it genuine.

quiz.question: AI is particularly useful for difficult emails because it removes the emotional charge from the task.
options: True
False
quiz.explanation: True. One of AI's most underrated email use cases is handling difficult messages — complaints, negotiations, awkward conversations. Because AI has no emotional reaction to the content, it produces calm, measured drafts that would take a human much longer to write when stressed or upset.

quiz.question: You receive a long, complex email from a client raising several concerns. What's the smartest AI workflow?
options: Ask AI to summarise the email first, then ask it to draft a reply addressing each concern
Ignore the email and hope the client follows up
Write the reply manually — AI can't handle complex multi-point emails
Forward the email to AI and ask it to reply directly on your behalf
quiz.explanation: Asking AI to summarise first ensures nothing is missed, then asking for a structured reply that addresses each concern produces a thorough, organised response. AI handles multi-point emails well — the key is telling it to address each point specifically rather than giving a general response.

quiz.question: Which of these is NOT a good use of AI for email?
options: Drafting a cold outreach email from bullet points
Rewriting a too-long email to be more concise
Sending emails automatically without human review
Writing a follow-up sequence for unanswered messages
quiz.explanation: AI should draft and improve emails — but a human should always review and approve before sending. Tone, accuracy, and appropriateness need your judgment. The other options are all excellent AI email use cases that save significant time.

lessons.title: AI Meeting Notes
lessons.subtitle: Never manually take meeting notes again — and get more from every meeting you attend

cards.headline: You can't fully listen to a meeting while taking notes. AI solves this completely.
cards.body: Meeting notes are one of the highest-value things AI can automate. Today you'll set up a system that captures everything, summarises it perfectly, and turns conversations into clear actions — automatically.
cards.statLabel: the average professional spends in meetings every week

cards.headline: The two approaches: real-time and post-meeting
cards.body: There are two ways to use AI for meeting notes. Both are powerful — you'll likely use both depending on the situation.
bullets: ⚡ Real-time tools (Otter.ai, Fireflies, Fathom) — join your call automatically, transcribe live, summarise instantly. Best for video calls.
📝 Post-meeting (ChatGPT / Claude) — paste in raw notes or a transcript and ask AI to structure them. Best when a live tool isn't available.
🎯 Either way, the output is the same: clean notes, key decisions, clear action items
💡 Fathom is free and excellent for Zoom and Google Meet

cards.headline: The post-meeting prompt that does the heavy lifting
cards.body: If you're working from rough notes or a transcript, this prompt consistently produces excellent structured summaries.
bullets: "Here are my raw notes from a [meeting type] with [attendees / context]:"
"[Paste your notes]"
"Please structure these into: 1) A 3-sentence summary, 2) Key decisions made, 3) Action items with owner and deadline, 4) Any open questions or next steps."
✅ You get a professional meeting record in under 30 seconds

cards.headline: Going further: AI before the meeting
cards.body: AI isn't just useful after a meeting. Using it beforehand can make the meeting itself dramatically more productive.
bullets: 📋 Agenda prep: "I'm running a 30-min product review with [team]. Create a tight agenda that covers [topics] and includes time for decisions."
💬 Pre-read summaries: paste a long document and ask for a 5-point briefing before the meeting
❓ Question generation: "I'm meeting a new client in [industry]. Generate 10 smart discovery questions."
⚡ Combining AI prep + AI notes is one of the biggest productivity unlocks available

cards.headline: Your task today
cards.body: Pick one of these two tasks based on what you have available right now:
bullets: 📝 Option A: Take your notes from any recent meeting and run them through the post-meeting prompt above. Compare the AI output to your original notes.
🆓 Option B: Sign up for Fathom (fathom.video — free) and connect it to your next video call. Let it run and see what it produces.
Either option will show you immediately how much time this saves

quiz.question: What is Fathom, and why was it mentioned in today's lesson?
options: An AI email tool that drafts replies automatically
A free AI note-taking tool that transcribes and summarises video calls in real time
A project management app with AI features
A Claude-powered document analyser
quiz.explanation: Fathom is a free AI meeting assistant that joins your Zoom, Google Meet, or Teams calls, transcribes them live, and produces an instant summary with action items afterwards. It's one of the most recommended free AI tools for professionals because it solves a high-pain problem at zero cost.

quiz.question: What are the four sections a well-structured AI meeting summary should include?
options: Attendance, agenda, discussion, and budget
Summary, key decisions, action items (with owner and deadline), and open questions
Introduction, main points, conclusion, and next meeting date
Goals, challenges, solutions, and outcomes
quiz.explanation: The four-section structure — summary, key decisions, action items with owner and deadline, open questions — produces a meeting record that is genuinely actionable. The most critical element is action items with a named owner and a deadline; without those, nothing gets done.

quiz.question: Using AI to prepare for a meeting (agenda, briefing, questions) is just as valuable as using it to capture notes afterwards.
options: True
False
quiz.explanation: True. AI before a meeting — generating tight agendas, summarising pre-reads, creating smart discovery questions — often has more impact than the notes themselves. A well-prepared meeting achieves more in less time. Combining AI prep and AI notes is a compounding productivity system.

quiz.question: You have rough, scattered notes from a meeting. What's the best AI workflow to turn them into something useful?
options: Type up a cleaner version of the notes manually, then use AI to format them
Paste the raw notes into ChatGPT or Claude and ask it to structure them into a summary, decisions, actions, and open questions
AI can't work with rough notes — it needs a proper transcript
Ask AI to guess what was discussed based on the meeting topic
quiz.explanation: You can paste rough, unstructured notes directly into AI and it will organise them. AI is excellent at finding the signal in noisy, informal notes. You don't need a clean transcript — the prompt does the structuring work for you.

lessons.title: AI Research Assistant
lessons.subtitle: Find, summarise, and synthesise information in minutes instead of hours

cards.headline: Research that used to take half a day now takes fifteen minutes. Here's exactly how.
cards.body: Whether you're researching a market, preparing for a meeting, learning about a competitor, or understanding a complex topic — AI has fundamentally changed how fast this can be done. Today you'll learn the workflows that make it happen.
cards.statLabel: to do what used to take half a day of research

cards.headline: The right tool for research: Perplexity
cards.body: For research that requires current, accurate, sourced information — Perplexity is the best tool available. Unlike ChatGPT, it searches the web in real time and cites every source.
bullets: 🔍 Searches the internet live — not limited to training data
📎 Cites sources for every claim — you can verify everything
📚 Summarises multiple sources into one clear answer
🆓 Free tier is excellent (perplexity.ai)
💡 Think of it as a research analyst who reads 20 articles and gives you the key points

cards.headline: Deep research with Claude or ChatGPT
cards.body: When you have documents, reports, or lengthy content to analyse rather than search for, Claude and ChatGPT are the right choice.
bullets: 📄 Upload PDFs, paste articles, or drop in long web pages
"Summarise this in 5 bullet points aimed at a non-expert"
"What are the three most important findings from this report?"
"Compare these two documents and highlight the key differences"
"What questions does this report leave unanswered?"
💡 Claude handles the longest documents best — up to book length in one session

cards.headline: Competitive and market research in minutes
cards.body: Some of the most powerful research prompts are for business intelligence. These work best in Perplexity (for live data) or ChatGPT with Browse enabled.
bullets: "Give me an overview of [competitor] — their product, positioning, pricing, and recent news"
"What are the top 5 trends in [industry] right now, with sources?"
"Summarise the key findings from recent research on [topic]"
"What do customers commonly complain about with [product/service category]? List the top pain points."
⚠️ Always check sources for anything business-critical — AI research is a starting point, not a final answer

cards.headline: Your task today
cards.body: Pick something you genuinely need to research right now — a competitor, a market, a topic for a meeting — and use this two-step workflow:
bullets: Step 1: Open Perplexity (perplexity.ai) and ask your research question. Review the sources it cites.
Step 2: Take the most useful article or result, paste it into Claude, and ask: "What are the 5 key takeaways from this, and what questions does it raise?"
You've just done in 10 minutes what would take most people 2 hours

quiz.question: Why is Perplexity better than standard ChatGPT for current research topics?
options: It has a better design and is easier to use
It searches the web in real time and cites its sources, unlike ChatGPT's static training data
It's faster at generating long responses
It's connected to academic databases that ChatGPT can't access
quiz.explanation: Perplexity searches the live internet and provides citations for every claim, making it far more reliable for current events, recent data, or any topic where accuracy and recency matter. ChatGPT's base model uses training data with a cutoff date and can't verify its own claims with sources.

quiz.question: You've been sent a 60-page industry report to review before a meeting tomorrow morning. What's the fastest AI workflow?
options: Use Perplexity to search for a summary of the report online
Ask ChatGPT to guess the contents based on the report title
Upload or paste the report into Claude and ask for the top findings, key decisions, and open questions
Read the report yourself — AI can't handle documents that long
quiz.explanation: Claude is purpose-built for exactly this. Its large context window handles lengthy documents comfortably, and asking for "top findings, key decisions, and open questions" produces a focused briefing that prepares you for the meeting in minutes rather than hours.

quiz.question: AI research results should always be treated as the final, verified answer.
options: True
False
quiz.explanation: False. AI research is a powerful starting point — it dramatically accelerates your understanding and highlights key information. But for anything business-critical, always verify important claims against the original sources. Even Perplexity, which cites its sources, can occasionally misinterpret or over-simplify what a source actually says.

quiz.question: Which prompt would give you the most useful competitive intelligence about a rival company?
options: "Tell me about [competitor]"
"Is [competitor] good?"
"Give me an overview of [competitor] — their product, positioning, pricing, recent news, and what customers say about them"
"Search the internet for [competitor]"
quiz.explanation: The specific, structured prompt — covering product, positioning, pricing, news, and customer sentiment — gives AI clear dimensions to research and report on. The vague alternatives will produce generic, unfocused results. Specificity in research prompts is just as important as in any other prompt type.

lessons.title: AI Writing Partner
lessons.subtitle: First drafts of anything — reports, proposals, blogs, briefs — in minutes, not hours

cards.headline: The blank page is the enemy of productivity. AI eliminates it entirely.
cards.body: Writer's block costs professionals an enormous amount of time. Whether it's a proposal, a report, a strategy document, or a blog post — AI can produce a solid first draft in under two minutes. Today you'll make that a permanent part of your workflow.
cards.statLabel: of professionals say writing tasks take longer than they should

cards.headline: The first-draft principle
cards.body: The single most powerful shift you can make: stop trying to write perfectly the first time. Use AI to generate a draft, then edit it into something great. Editing is always faster than writing from scratch.
bullets: 🧠 Your job is now editor, not writer — a much easier task
⚡ AI produces a 500-word draft in under 10 seconds
✍️ You spend 5–10 minutes shaping it into your voice
📄 Total time for a solid piece of writing: under 15 minutes
💡 Even if you change 70% of the draft, AI still saved you the hardest part — starting

cards.headline: The writing prompt that works for almost anything
cards.body: This flexible template produces a usable first draft for reports, proposals, emails, articles, briefs, and more.
bullets: "Act as an expert [role: business writer / consultant / journalist]."
"Write a [document type] about [topic]."
"Audience: [who will read this]."
"Key points to cover: [bullet list]."
"Length: approximately [X] words."
"Tone: [professional / conversational / persuasive / authoritative]."
💡 The more specific your bullet points, the better the draft

cards.headline: Making AI writing sound like you
cards.body: Generic AI writing is easy to spot — and easy to fix. These techniques make AI output sound like it came from you.
bullets: 📝 Paste in a sample of your own writing: "Match the tone and style of this example: [paste]"
✂️ Read it aloud — anything that feels stiff, rewrite in one sentence
🎯 Add one specific detail or personal observation AI couldn't know
💬 Replace corporate phrases ("leverage synergies") with plain language
🔄 Ask AI to "make this sound less like AI and more like a real person wrote it"

cards.headline: Your task today
cards.body: Pick one piece of writing you've been putting off — a report, a proposal, a blog post, an update — and use AI to get the first draft done right now.
bullets: Use the writing prompt template above
Give it at least 4–5 bullet points of key content to cover
Read the draft, make your edits, and finish it
Notice: you've just completed something you'd been avoiding

quiz.question: What is the "first-draft principle" and why does it matter?
options: AI should write the final version — humans shouldn't edit it
Use AI to generate a rough draft, then edit it — editing is always faster than writing from scratch
Always write the first draft yourself before involving AI
The first draft should be the shortest version of the document
quiz.explanation: The first-draft principle is about eliminating the hardest part of writing — starting. AI gives you a foundation to edit and shape, which is significantly faster than writing from scratch. Even if you change 70% of the draft, AI still saved you the blank-page problem.

quiz.question: Which technique best helps AI writing sound like it came from you personally?
options: Using longer, more detailed prompts
Asking AI to write in a formal academic style
Pasting in a sample of your own writing and asking AI to match the tone and style
Using a different AI tool for writing tasks
quiz.explanation: Providing a sample of your own writing as a style reference is one of the most effective ways to get AI output that sounds like you. AI is excellent at analysing and replicating writing style — the trick is giving it an example to work from, rather than describing the style abstractly.

quiz.question: AI-generated writing never needs to be edited by a human before it's published or sent.
options: True
False
quiz.explanation: False. AI writing always benefits from human editing — for accuracy, personal voice, specific details AI couldn't know, and removing any phrases that sound overly corporate or generic. Your role shifts from writer to editor, which is faster and easier, but the editing step is essential.

quiz.question: You need to write a 1,000-word business proposal for a potential client. What's the most efficient AI workflow?
options: Ask AI to write the whole thing with no further input and send it as-is
Write it all yourself, then ask AI to proofread
Give AI a detailed prompt with key points to cover, edit the draft to add your voice and specific client details, then finalise
Use AI to write one paragraph at a time with separate prompts for each
quiz.explanation: A detailed prompt with key points produces a coherent, structured draft quickly. Editing that draft to add your voice, specific client context, and personal insight produces a high-quality final proposal in a fraction of the time writing from scratch would take.

lessons.title: AI Task Planner
lessons.subtitle: Build a smarter, more realistic daily plan — and actually stick to it

cards.headline: Most to-do lists fail not because people are lazy — but because the list was never realistic to begin with.
cards.body: AI doesn't just help you work faster — it helps you plan smarter. Today you'll build an AI-powered daily planning system that creates realistic schedules, prioritises ruthlessly, and adapts when things inevitably change.
cards.statLabel: of tasks on to-do lists are never completed

cards.headline: The daily planning prompt
cards.body: Start every morning (or the night before) with this prompt. It takes 60 seconds and produces a plan you can actually follow.
bullets: "I have [X hours] available today."
"My tasks are: [paste your list]."
"My top priority outcome for today is: [one thing]."
"Please organise these into a realistic time-blocked schedule, grouping similar tasks and protecting [1–2 hours] for deep work in the morning."
💡 Add "I have a meeting at [time]" and AI will build the plan around it

cards.headline: Prioritisation: cut the list, not the quality
cards.body: Most people's task lists are too long. AI is ruthlessly honest about what actually needs doing today — something humans struggle with.
bullets: "Here are my 15 tasks for today. I have 4 hours. Which 5 should I focus on, and why?"
"Which of these tasks could be delegated, automated, or deleted entirely?"
"What's the one task on this list that would make everything else easier or irrelevant?"
💡 This last question is from Gary Keller's The ONE Thing — AI applies it perfectly

cards.headline: When the plan falls apart (and it will)
cards.body: Every plan hits reality. AI helps you recover quickly rather than abandoning the day entirely.
bullets: "It's 2pm, I've only done [X] from my plan. I have [Y hours] left. Rebuild my afternoon."
"I've just been given an urgent task. Help me reprioritise the rest of my day around it."
"I'm feeling overwhelmed and don't know where to start. Here's my list — help me pick just one thing."
🎯 The goal isn't a perfect day — it's a recovered day. AI makes that easy.

cards.headline: Your task today
cards.body: Use the daily planning prompt on your actual tasks for tomorrow. Do it tonight so you start tomorrow with clarity instead of chaos.
bullets: Write out everything you need to do tomorrow — brain dump it all
Paste it into ChatGPT or Claude with the daily planning prompt
Review the schedule it creates and adjust anything that feels wrong
Save the output as your plan for tomorrow — then follow it

quiz.question: What makes AI-generated daily plans more realistic than lists humans make themselves?
options: AI has access to your calendar and can see your actual availability
AI applies time constraints objectively, without the optimism bias humans have about how much they can do
AI plans always include breaks, which humans forget to schedule
AI plans are automatically synced to your task management app
quiz.explanation: Humans consistently overestimate what they can accomplish in a day — a well-documented cognitive bias called planning fallacy. AI, given a specific time constraint, allocates tasks more objectively. By forcing you to specify available hours upfront, it creates a plan grounded in reality rather than optimism.

quiz.question: You have 15 tasks but only 4 hours. What's the most effective AI prompt to use?
options: "Complete all 15 of my tasks as fast as possible"
"Here are my 15 tasks. I have 4 hours. Which 5 should I focus on and why?"
"Make my 15 tasks go faster"
"Tell me which tasks are important"
quiz.explanation: Asking AI to select and justify the top 5 tasks from 15 — given a specific time constraint — forces ruthless prioritisation with clear reasoning. The justification ("and why") is crucial: it helps you decide whether to accept AI's reasoning or override it based on context AI doesn't have.

quiz.question: If your plan falls apart mid-day, the best approach is to abandon it and start fresh tomorrow.
options: True
False
quiz.explanation: False. A mid-day recovery prompt — telling AI what you've done, what time you have left, and asking it to rebuild the afternoon — is one of the highest-value daily AI habits. Most productive days aren't perfectly executed plans; they're plans that were recovered when they went off track.

quiz.question: What does "The ONE Thing" question — "What's the one task that would make everything else easier or irrelevant?" — help you do?
options: Delete unnecessary tasks from your list
Identify the single highest-leverage task and protect time for it above everything else
Ask AI to complete the most important task automatically
Schedule the hardest task for last to build momentum
quiz.explanation: This question — popularised by Gary Keller — cuts through noise to find the task with the highest leverage. Completing it often makes other tasks unnecessary, easier, or less urgent. AI applies this filter precisely when you give it your full task list, consistently surfacing the most important work.

lessons.title: AI Decision Maker
lessons.subtitle: Use AI as a thinking partner to make better decisions faster — with less stress

cards.headline: The average person makes 35,000 decisions a day. Most are fine. But the big ones deserve a thinking partner.
cards.body: AI is one of the best thinking partners available for big, complex, or emotionally charged decisions. It's patient, has no agenda, and can hold far more variables in its head than any single human. Today you'll learn how to use it well.
cards.statLabel: decisions made by the average person every single day

cards.headline: Why AI is a great decision partner
cards.body: Humans make worse decisions when they're tired, stressed, or emotionally invested. AI has none of those limitations.
bullets: 🧠 No emotional stake — it analyses without fear, ego, or hope
📊 Handles complexity — it can consider many variables simultaneously
🔍 Asks the questions you didn't think to ask
⚖️ Plays devil's advocate without worrying about hurting your feelings
🔄 Available at 2am when you're lying awake overthinking

cards.headline: The decision framework prompt
cards.body: This prompt structure works for any significant decision — career moves, business choices, financial decisions, major purchases.
bullets: "I'm trying to decide between [Option A] and [Option B]."
"Context: [your situation in 3–5 sentences]."
"My priorities are: [list what matters most to you]."
"Think step by step. Lay out the pros and cons of each option, flag any risks I might not have considered, and give me your honest recommendation."
💡 The "honest recommendation" part is key — don't let AI dodge the question

cards.headline: Three powerful decision techniques
cards.body: Beyond the basic framework, these three prompts are particularly useful for specific decision challenges.
bullets: 😈 Devil's advocate: "Give me the strongest possible argument AGAINST the decision I'm leaning towards."
⏩ Pre-mortem: "Assume I take Option A and it fails badly 12 months from now. What went wrong?"
👴 The 10/10/10 test: "How will I feel about this decision in 10 minutes, 10 months, and 10 years?"
🎯 Use all three on any decision you're genuinely torn about — it takes 10 minutes and removes most of the fog

cards.headline: Your task today
cards.body: Think of a decision you've been sitting on — big or small. Run it through AI right now.
bullets: Use the decision framework prompt with your real options and context
Then run the devil's advocate prompt on the option you're leaning towards
Notice whether AI surfaces anything you hadn't considered
💡 You don't have to take AI's advice — the value is in the structured thinking process

quiz.question: What is a "pre-mortem" in the context of decision-making?
options: A checklist you complete before making any decision
Imagining that a decision has already failed and working backwards to identify what went wrong
Asking AI to approve a decision before you make it
A review of past decisions to learn from mistakes
quiz.explanation: A pre-mortem — popularised by psychologist Gary Klein — involves projecting yourself into the future, assuming the decision failed, and asking "what went wrong?" It's far more effective than asking "what could go wrong?" because it bypasses optimism bias and forces concrete failure scenarios. AI performs pre-mortems exceptionally well.

quiz.question: Why is AI particularly well-suited as a decision-making partner compared to asking a human friend or colleague?
options: AI always makes the right decision
AI has no emotional stake, no agenda, and can process more variables without getting overwhelmed
AI has access to data that humans don't
AI decisions are legally binding, which creates accountability
quiz.explanation: AI's value as a decision partner comes from what it lacks: ego, fear, emotional investment, and fatigue. It analyses options objectively, asks questions you might have avoided, and gives honest assessments without worrying about your reaction. This makes it especially valuable for emotionally charged decisions.

quiz.question: The 10/10/10 test asks you to consider how you'll feel about a decision in 10 minutes, 10 months, and 10 years.
options: True
False
quiz.explanation: True. The 10/10/10 framework (from Suzy Welch) creates temporal distance from a decision, reducing the emotional intensity of the immediate moment. Short-term regret and long-term regret are very different things — and AI applies this framework clearly when asked, helping you see which timeframe matters most for your specific situation.

quiz.question: You ask AI for its recommendation between two options. It gives a balanced "both have pros and cons" non-answer. What should you do?
options: Accept that AI can't make this decision and rely on your gut instead
Push back: ask AI to give you its honest recommendation and explain its reasoning
Flip a coin — both options are equally good
Ask a different AI tool for a second opinion
quiz.explanation: AI sometimes defaults to balanced, non-committal answers to avoid seeming biased. Push back explicitly: "I understand both have merits — if you had to recommend one, which would it be and why?" This almost always produces a clearer, more useful answer. Asking for the reasoning is as valuable as the recommendation itself.

✍️ Before writing: always get a first draft from AI, then edit
💡 The goal is to make these reflexes, not rituals — automatic, not deliberate

Save or screenshot the output — this is your personal AI operating system

quiz.question: What is the key difference between an AI productivity "ritual" and an AI productivity "reflex"?
options: Rituals use ChatGPT; reflexes use Claude
A ritual is something you deliberately schedule; a reflex is an automatic habit you do without thinking
Rituals are for morning tasks; reflexes are for afternoon tasks
There is no meaningful difference
quiz.explanation: The goal of building a productivity stack is to make AI use automatic — a reflex triggered by a situation (writing = open AI first, meeting ends = run notes through summary prompt). Rituals require willpower to maintain; reflexes are just how you work. Getting there takes a few weeks of deliberate practice.

quiz.question: Which of the following best describes a personal AI productivity stack?
options: A paid subscription bundle for multiple AI tools
A consistent set of AI tools and workflows that work together to handle recurring tasks automatically
A folder of saved prompts organised by category
A daily to-do list generated by AI each morning
quiz.explanation: A productivity stack is a system — specific tools matched to specific tasks, triggered by specific situations. The consistency is what makes it powerful. Once it's set up and habitual, you stop making decisions about whether to use AI and just use it, compounding the time savings every day.

quiz.question: The best time to run your daily planning prompt is first thing in the morning on the day itself.
options: True
False

This means you start the next day with a clear plan already in place — no decision fatigue in the morning, no time wasted figuring out what to work on. Starting the day with clarity is one of the highest-leverage productivity habits.

quiz.question: For internet research, which tool should you reach for first according to your productivity stack?
options: Google — it's the most comprehensive search engine
ChatGPT — it's the most versatile AI tool
Perplexity — it searches the live web and cites its sources
Claude — it has the largest context window
