For research questions, it's almost always faster and more comprehensive than starting with Google. Claude is better for analysing documents you already have; Perplexity is better for finding and synthesising new information.

lessons.title: AI Image Creation
lessons.subtitle: Create professional-quality visuals in seconds — no design skills, no designer required

cards.headline: A year ago, creating a professional image took hours and a designer. Today it takes 30 seconds and a sentence.
cards.body: AI image generation has quietly become one of the most commercially valuable skills you can have. Whether you need social media visuals, product mockups, blog headers, or brand imagery — AI creates them instantly. Today you'll master the tools and the prompts.
cards.statLabel: to generate a professional-quality image from a text description

cards.headline: The three image tools you need to know
cards.body: The AI image market has matured rapidly. Three tools lead the field — each with different strengths.
bullets: 🎨 Midjourney — the gold standard for artistic, high-quality images. Stunning results, especially for people, scenes, and brand imagery. Requires Discord (from ~$10/mo).
⚡ DALL·E 3 (built into ChatGPT) — the most convenient option. Type your prompt in ChatGPT and get an image instantly. Free tier available.
🔥 Flux — the newest benchmark for photorealistic images. Increasingly preferred by professionals for commercial work. Available via Leonardo.ai (free tier).
💡 Start with DALL·E 3 in ChatGPT — zero setup, free, and produces excellent results for most use cases

cards.headline: Writing image prompts that actually work
cards.body: Image prompts are different to text prompts — they need to describe what you see, not what you want to achieve. Think like a film director describing a shot.
bullets: 🖼️ Subject — what's in the image ("a confident woman at a laptop")
🎨 Style — the visual feel ("photorealistic", "minimalist flat illustration", "cinematic")
💡 Lighting — massively affects quality ("golden hour light", "soft studio lighting", "moody overhead")
🎭 Mood — the emotion ("energetic and modern", "calm and professional", "bold and striking")
📐 Composition — how it's framed ("wide shot", "close-up portrait", "overhead flat lay")
💡 Example: "A confident professional woman working at a modern desk, soft natural window light, minimalist office background, photorealistic, warm tones"

cards.headline: Practical use cases that save real money
cards.body: Here's where AI image creation pays for itself immediately — tasks that previously required a designer or stock photo subscription.
bullets: 📱 Social media graphics — custom images matched to your brand in seconds
📝 Blog and article headers — relevant, unique visuals instead of generic stock photos
🛍️ Product mockups — show products in lifestyle settings before they exist
📊 Presentation visuals — custom illustrations that make slides look designed
🎨 Brand mood boards — explore visual directions without hiring a creative agency
💡 For commercial use, always check the tool's licensing terms

cards.headline: Your task today
cards.body: Create your first AI image for something you actually need — a social post, a blog header, a presentation slide.
bullets: Open ChatGPT (free) and start a new conversation
Type: "Generate an image of [your subject], [style], [lighting], [mood]"
If you don't love the result, add "Make it more [X]" or "Regenerate with [change]"
Save the image and use it somewhere real this week

quiz.question: Which AI image tool is built directly into ChatGPT and requires no additional setup?
options: Midjourney
Flux
DALL·E 3
Stable Diffusion
quiz.explanation: DALL·E 3 is OpenAI's image model and is built directly into ChatGPT. You simply describe what you want in a chat message and the image is generated inline. It's the lowest-friction way to start with AI image generation — no new tools, no Discord, no separate account needed.

quiz.question: When writing an image prompt, which element has the single biggest impact on the quality and feel of the result?
options: The number of words in the prompt
Specifying the exact pixel dimensions
Lighting description — it fundamentally shapes mood, realism, and visual quality
Using technical photography terms like "f/1.8 aperture"
quiz.explanation: Lighting is often the most transformative element in an image prompt. "Soft natural window light" vs "harsh overhead fluorescent" vs "golden hour warm glow" produces completely different results with the same subject. Professional photographers know lighting makes or breaks a shot — the same applies to AI image generation.

quiz.question: AI-generated images can be used for any commercial purpose without restriction.
options: True
False
quiz.explanation: False. Each AI image tool has its own licensing terms, which vary by tool and subscription tier. Midjourney's free tier, for example, doesn't allow commercial use. DALL·E 3 generally allows commercial use of generated images. Always check the specific terms of the tool you're using before using images commercially.

quiz.question: Which of these is the most effective image prompt for generating a professional social media graphic?
options: "A good social media image"
"Make something for Instagram"
"A confident entrepreneur at a modern laptop, soft studio lighting, clean white background, photorealistic, professional and aspirational mood"
"Professional image, high quality, good colours"
quiz.explanation: The detailed prompt specifies subject, environment, lighting, background, style, and mood — giving the AI clear visual directions. Vague prompts produce generic, unusable results. The more specific and visual your description, the closer the output will be to what you actually need.

lessons.title: AI Social Media
lessons.subtitle: Plan, write, and schedule a full week of social content in under 10 minutes

cards.headline: Consistent social media presence is one of the most powerful business tools available. Most people fail at it because it's time-consuming. AI removes that excuse entirely.
cards.body: The biggest barrier to social media isn't knowing what to say — it's the time it takes to say it consistently. Today you'll build a content workflow that produces a week's worth of posts in a single 10-minute session.
cards.statLabel: to plan and write an entire week of social content with AI

cards.headline: The content pillar system
cards.body: The most effective social media strategies are built on 3–4 content pillars — recurring themes that define what you talk about. AI uses these to generate varied, on-brand content at scale.
bullets: 🎓 Educational — tips, how-tos, explainers ("Did you know...")
💬 Personal/Story — behind the scenes, lessons learned, your journey
🏆 Social proof — results, testimonials, case studies
📣 Promotional — offers, products, calls to action (use sparingly — max 20%)
💡 Define your 3–4 pillars once, then AI generates content within them indefinitely

cards.headline: The weekly content batch prompt
cards.body: This is the prompt that replaces hours of content planning with a 10-minute session. Run it once a week.
bullets: "Act as a social media strategist. I am [your name/role] in [your industry/niche]."
"My audience is [describe them]. My content pillars are: [list yours]."
"Write 5 social media posts for [platform: LinkedIn / Instagram / X / TikTok script]."
"Mix the pillars across the 5 posts. Each post should have a hook, value, and a clear CTA."
"Tone: [your tone — e.g. direct and expert / warm and encouraging / bold and punchy]."
💡 Add "include relevant hashtags" and "suggest the best day/time to post each" for a complete plan

cards.headline: Platform-specific rules AI needs to know
cards.body: Each platform has a different format, audience expectation, and algorithm. Tell AI which platform you're writing for — it changes everything.
bullets: 💼 LinkedIn: professional tone, longer posts perform well (150–300 words), personal stories get high engagement, no more than 3 hashtags
📸 Instagram: visual-first, shorter captions or long storytelling, 5–10 hashtags, strong opening line
🐦 X (Twitter): punchy and conversational, under 280 characters or threaded, opinions and hot takes perform well
🎵 TikTok/Reels: write a script, not a caption — hook in first 2 seconds, spoken word, trend-aware
💡 Always specify the platform — "write a LinkedIn post" vs "write a post" produces completely different results

cards.headline: Your task today
cards.body: Run your first weekly content batch right now. You'll have 5 ready-to-post pieces of content within 10 minutes.
bullets: Define your 3 content pillars (write them down — you'll use these every week)
Run the weekly content batch prompt for your main platform
Review the 5 posts, edit for your voice, and schedule or save them
💡 Tools like Buffer and Later (both have free tiers) let you schedule posts in advance — AI writes, you schedule once a week

quiz.question: What are "content pillars" and why do they matter for AI social media content?
options: The visual columns in an Instagram grid layout
Recurring content themes that define what you post about, giving AI a consistent framework to generate varied on-brand content
The number of posts you publish per week
AI-generated hashtag categories for organising content
quiz.explanation: Content pillars are recurring themes — Educational, Personal, Social Proof, Promotional — that form the backbone of a consistent content strategy. Once defined, they give AI a clear brief to work within, producing varied posts that all feel on-brand. Defining them once means AI can generate content for you indefinitely.

quiz.question: You're writing posts for LinkedIn. Which style instruction is most appropriate?
options: Short, punchy captions under 50 words with trending audio suggestions
Professional tone, 150–300 words, personal story structure, maximum 3 hashtags
Casual and humorous, heavy use of emojis, 10+ hashtags
Formal academic writing style, no hashtags, dense paragraphs
quiz.explanation: LinkedIn favours professional but personal content — posts that share genuine insight, experiences, or lessons tend to outperform purely promotional or overly formal content. The algorithm rewards engagement, and personal stories consistently drive high engagement on the platform. Always specify platform-specific guidance in your content prompts.

quiz.question: Promotional content (offers, products, CTAs) should make up the majority of your social media posts.
options: True
False
quiz.explanation: False. A widely used guideline is the 80/20 rule — 80% valuable, educational, or entertaining content; 20% promotional. Audiences follow and engage with accounts that give them value. If every post is selling something, people unfollow. Build trust and authority with valuable content; your promotional posts will then perform far better.

quiz.question: What is the most important structural element of a social media post according to today's lesson?
options: The hashtags — they determine who sees the post
The image — visuals always outperform text-only posts
The hook — the opening line that stops the scroll and makes people read further
The CTA — without it, posts have no purpose
quiz.explanation: The hook — the opening line or first 2 seconds — is the single most important element of any social post. On every platform, users are scrolling fast. If the first line doesn't stop them, nothing else matters. When briefing AI, always ask for a strong hook specifically, and review it carefully before anything else.

lessons.title: AI Video Scripts
lessons.subtitle: Write scroll-stopping scripts for TikTok, Reels, and YouTube Shorts — in minutes

cards.headline: Short-form video is the most powerful distribution channel on the planet right now. AI makes the hardest part — the script — effortless.
cards.body: TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts collectively serve over 3 billion views per day. The creators winning that attention all have one thing in common: they understand structure. Today you'll learn how to write that structure with AI in minutes.
cards.statLabel: short-form video views served every single day

cards.headline: The anatomy of a viral short-form script
cards.body: Viral short-form videos follow a remarkably consistent structure. Once you know it, you'll see it everywhere — and AI can execute it perfectly every time.
bullets: ⚡ Hook (0–3 sec) — a bold statement, controversial opinion, or direct promise that stops the scroll
🎯 Relate (3–8 sec) — show you understand their problem or situation
💡 Value (8–45 sec) — deliver the insight, tip, or story — fast, no padding
🔄 Retain (throughout) — pattern interrupts, questions, "but here's the thing…"
📣 CTA (final 3 sec) — one clear action: follow, comment, save, or visit
💡 The entire script should be speakable in under 60 seconds — cut anything that doesn't earn its place

cards.headline: The short-form script prompt
cards.body: This prompt produces a ready-to-film script that follows the proven viral structure.
bullets: "Act as a viral short-form video scriptwriter."
"Write a 45–60 second script for [TikTok / Instagram Reels / YouTube Shorts]."
"Topic: [your topic or insight]."
"Target audience: [describe them]."
"Hook style: [bold statement / surprising stat / controversial opinion / direct promise]."
"Tone: [energetic / calm expert / storytelling / punchy]."
"End with a CTA to [follow / comment / save / visit link]."
💡 Ask for 3 alternative hook options — hooks are everything, so having choices is worth it

cards.headline: Repurposing: one idea, five formats
cards.body: The smartest content creators don't create five pieces of content — they create one idea and reformat it five ways. AI makes this nearly instant.
bullets: 🎬 Start with your short-form script
💼 "Rewrite this as a LinkedIn post" — professional, insight-led
📸 "Give me 5 Instagram carousel slide titles from this content"
🐦 "Compress the key insight into a punchy 240-character X post"
📧 "Expand this into a 300-word email newsletter intro"
💡 One 10-minute AI session = a week of multi-platform content from a single idea

cards.headline: Your task today
cards.body: Write your first AI video script on a topic you actually know something about.
bullets: Think of one genuine insight, tip, or lesson from your work or life
Run the short-form script prompt above
Ask for 3 alternative hook options and pick the strongest one
Read it aloud — does it sound natural? Edit anything that feels forced
🎬 Bonus: film it. You don't need to post it — just see how a scripted video feels vs. improvising

quiz.question: In the short-form video structure, what is the purpose of the "Hook" and how long should it be?
options: Introduce yourself and your credentials — takes about 10–15 seconds
Stop the scroll with a bold statement or direct promise — must land in the first 3 seconds
Summarise the whole video so viewers know what to expect — about 5–8 seconds
State the problem the video solves — takes the first 10 seconds
quiz.explanation: The hook must do its job in the first 2–3 seconds — that's the average window before a viewer scrolls past. It should be bold, surprising, or directly address something the target viewer cares about. Self-introductions and slow build-ups consistently kill watch time on short-form platforms.

quiz.question: What is "content repurposing" and why does AI make it so powerful?
options: Re-posting the same video on multiple platforms without any changes
Taking one core idea and reformatting it into multiple content types for different platforms — AI makes this nearly instant
Using AI to find and repost other creators' popular content
Scheduling the same post to go live at different times across the week
quiz.explanation: Repurposing means extracting maximum value from a single idea by reformatting it for different platforms and audiences. What takes a content team hours — adapting a video script into a LinkedIn post, carousel, tweet, and email — AI does in under two minutes. It's one of the highest-leverage content workflows available.

quiz.question: A short-form video script should be as long and detailed as possible to deliver maximum value.
options: True
False
quiz.explanation: False. Short-form video thrives on brevity and pace. Scripts should be speakable in under 60 seconds, with every sentence earning its place. Padding kills watch time, and low watch time kills reach. AI is actually excellent at cutting scripts down when prompted — "make this tighter" consistently improves short-form scripts.

quiz.question: You want to maximise the impact of a single piece of AI-generated content. What's the best approach?
options: Post the same video on every platform simultaneously without changes
Choose one platform and focus all content there
Use AI to reformat the core idea into platform-specific versions for LinkedIn, Instagram, X, and email
Create entirely separate content for each platform from scratch
quiz.explanation: Platform-specific reformatting — not identical cross-posting — is the highest-leverage content approach. Each platform has different norms, formats, and audiences. AI rewrites the same core idea into versions optimised for each platform in minutes, giving you multi-platform presence from a single creative session.

lessons.title: AI Copywriting
lessons.subtitle: Write landing pages, ads, and emails that persuade and convert — using proven frameworks

cards.headline: Copywriting is the skill that turns attention into action. AI now gives everyone access to it.
cards.body: Great copy — the words on your website, in your ads, in your emails — is the difference between a business that grows and one that flatlines. Professional copywriters charge thousands of pounds per project. Today you'll learn to produce the same quality output yourself, using AI and proven frameworks.
cards.statLabel: typical cost of a professional copywriter for a landing page — AI does it in minutes

cards.headline: The PAS framework: the most reliable copy structure ever written
cards.body: Problem–Agitate–Solution. Used by every great copywriter for over 50 years. AI executes it perfectly when you provide the right inputs.
bullets: 😓 Problem — name the exact pain your audience is experiencing ("You're spending 3 hours on emails every day")
🔥 Agitate — make the pain feel real and urgent ("That's 15 hours a week, 60 hours a month, wasted on a task that isn't moving your business forward")
✅ Solution — present your product/service/offer as the obvious answer ("SuccessWise shows you how to cut that to 30 minutes — starting today")
💡 Prompt: "Write [copy type] using the PAS framework for [your product/service]. The problem is [X], the agitation is [Y], the solution is [Z]."

cards.headline: The AIDA framework: from stranger to buyer
cards.body: Attention–Interest–Desire–Action. The structure behind almost every effective ad, email, and landing page. It maps perfectly onto the journey from "who are you?" to "take my money."
bullets: 👁️ Attention — the headline that stops them ("Most people waste 15 hours a week on email")
💡 Interest — why this matters to them specifically ("Research shows knowledge workers lose 3 hours daily to inbox management")
❤️ Desire — paint the picture of life with your solution ("Imagine finishing your emails in 30 minutes and spending the rest of your day on work that actually matters")
👆 Action — one clear, low-friction step ("Start free today — no credit card required")
💡 Use AIDA for ad copy, email sequences, and landing page sections

cards.headline: Headlines: the 80/20 of copywriting
cards.body: Eight out of ten people read the headline. Only two read the rest. Your headline is 80% of the copy's value — treat it accordingly.
bullets: 🔢 Numbers work: "7 ways to…", "The 3-minute trick that…", "How 4,800 people…"
❓ Questions create curiosity: "Are you making these 5 AI mistakes?"
⚡ Specificity builds credibility: "Save 10 hours a week" beats "Save time"
🎯 Address the reader directly: "For people who want to X without Y"
💡 Prompt: "Write 10 alternative headlines for [offer/product]. Use different styles: number-based, question, direct promise, curiosity, and social proof."

cards.headline: Your task today
cards.body: Pick one thing you need to sell or promote — a product, a service, yourself, or an idea. Write copy for it using both frameworks.
bullets: Round 1: "Write a 100-word product description for [X] using the PAS framework. The problem is [X], the agitation is [Y], the solution is [Z]."
Round 2: "Now rewrite it using the AIDA framework."
Round 3: "Write 10 headline options for this product using different styles."
Compare both versions — notice how the frameworks produce different emotional pulls

quiz.question: In the PAS copywriting framework, what does "Agitate" mean?
options: Introduce a new problem the reader didn't know they had
Make the existing problem feel more real, urgent, and costly before presenting the solution
Criticise competing products to make yours look better
Use urgent language like "limited time offer" to pressure the reader
quiz.explanation: Agitation deepens the reader's awareness of the pain they already feel. It's not about manufacturing new fears — it's about making the existing problem feel vivid and urgent enough that the solution feels necessary, not optional. Done well, it makes the reader feel understood before you even present what you're selling.

quiz.question: According to research on reading behaviour, roughly what percentage of people read the headline of a piece of copy?
quiz.explanation: 80% of readers read the headline; only 20% go further. This is why professional copywriters routinely spend more time on headlines than on the body copy. When using AI for copywriting, always ask for multiple headline options and choose carefully — it's where most of the persuasive work happens.

quiz.question: The AIDA framework stands for Attention, Information, Discussion, and Action.
options: True
False
quiz.explanation: False. AIDA stands for Attention, Interest, Desire, Action. It maps the psychological journey a prospect takes from first encountering your message to taking action. Each stage has a specific job: Attention stops them, Interest makes them care, Desire makes them want it, Action tells them what to do next.

quiz.question: Which of these headline techniques tends to be most effective for building immediate credibility?
options: Vague, mysterious headlines that create curiosity
Long headlines that explain everything upfront
Specific numbers and concrete outcomes ("Save 10 hours a week" vs "Save time")
All-caps headlines for emphasis
quiz.explanation: Specificity is one of the most reliable credibility signals in copywriting. "Save 10 hours a week" is more believable than "Save time" because the specificity implies it's been measured. "Used by 4,800 learners" beats "popular course" for the same reason. When using AI for headlines, always push for specific numbers over vague claims.

lessons.title: AI Presentation Maker
lessons.subtitle: Build compelling slide decks in under 30 minutes — structure, content, and visuals included

cards.headline: A great presentation can change a career, close a deal, or launch a business. AI now builds them in under 30 minutes.
cards.body: Most people spend hours agonising over slide structure and bullet points. AI handles both — leaving you to focus on delivery, which is the part that actually determines whether the presentation lands.
cards.statLabel: from blank page to complete, compelling slide deck with AI

cards.headline: Step 1: let AI design the structure
cards.body: The biggest presentation mistake is jumping straight into slides before the structure is clear. AI designs logical, compelling structures faster than any human — start here.
bullets: "Act as a presentation strategist. I need to create a [X-minute] presentation on [topic] for [audience]."
"The goal of this presentation is to [inform / persuade / sell / inspire]."
"Design a slide-by-slide structure. For each slide, give me: the slide title, the key message, and 2–3 bullet points of content."
💡 This gives you a complete blueprint before you open PowerPoint, Keynote, or Google Slides

cards.headline: Step 2: generate slide content
cards.body: Once your structure is approved, use AI to write the content for each slide. The key principle: one idea per slide, expressed in as few words as possible.
bullets: "Write the content for slide [X]: [slide title]. Key message: [what it needs to communicate]."
"Give me a headline (max 8 words) and 3 bullet points (max 12 words each)."
🚫 Never put a paragraph on a slide — slides are prompts for your speech, not scripts
✅ The rule: if you can't say the slide's key message in one sentence, it needs splitting into two slides
💡 Ask AI: "Is this slide trying to say too much? How would you split it?"

cards.headline: Step 3: use AI tools that build the whole deck
cards.body: If you want AI to actually build the slides — not just the content — several tools now do this end-to-end.
bullets: 🎨 Gamma (gamma.app) — paste your outline and it generates a beautifully designed deck instantly. Free tier available. Best for most use cases.
📊 Beautiful.ai — AI-powered slide design that adjusts layouts automatically
🖼️ Tome — narrative-focused presentations with AI-generated visuals built in
💡 Workflow: use ChatGPT/Claude to build the structure and content → paste into Gamma → customise the design → done in 30 minutes
⚠️ Always review AI-generated designs — they're excellent starting points but may need brand adjustments

cards.headline: Your task today
cards.body: Build an AI presentation on something you actually need — a project update, a pitch, a training session, or even a personal topic.
bullets: Use the structure prompt to get a complete slide-by-slide blueprint
Review the structure — add, remove, or reorder slides as needed
Open Gamma (gamma.app) and paste your structure to generate the visual deck
Share it with one person and get their honest reaction

quiz.question: What is the most important step to complete before building any individual slides?
options: Choose the visual theme and colour scheme
Design the full slide-by-slide structure and key message for each slide
Write all the speaker notes
Find images and graphics for each slide
quiz.explanation: Structure first, always. The most common presentation mistake is opening a slide tool and building slides before the overall logic is clear. A well-structured deck with average design is far more effective than a beautifully designed deck with poor structure. AI builds logical structures quickly — use it before touching a single slide.

quiz.question: What is the "one idea per slide" principle?
options: Every slide should contain exactly one bullet point
Each slide should communicate a single clear message — if it's trying to say two things, split it into two slides
Use only one font throughout the entire presentation
The first slide should introduce the one main idea, and the rest should repeat it
quiz.explanation: The one idea per slide principle keeps presentations clear and audiences engaged. When a slide tries to communicate multiple things simultaneously, the audience's attention splits and nothing lands clearly. If you can't state a slide's key message in one sentence, it needs splitting. AI applies this principle well when explicitly asked to.

quiz.question: Slides should contain as much text as possible so the audience can read along with you.
options: True
False
quiz.explanation: False. Text-heavy slides are one of the most common presentation mistakes. When audiences read the slides, they stop listening to you. Slides should contain the minimum text needed to prompt your speech — short headlines, brief bullets. The detail lives in what you say, not what's written on screen.

quiz.question: Which AI tool is specifically designed to turn a text outline into a visually designed presentation deck automatically?
options: ChatGPT — it can generate slide images directly
Perplexity — it researches and designs slides simultaneously
Gamma — it converts a text outline into a designed deck instantly
Claude — it produces PowerPoint files directly
quiz.explanation: Gamma (gamma.app) is purpose-built for this workflow: paste your content outline, and it generates a professionally designed presentation deck. It's one of the most impressive AI presentation tools available and has a generous free tier. The recommended workflow is ChatGPT/Claude for structure and content → Gamma for design.

lessons.title: AI Audio & Voice

cards.headline: A podcast episode that used to take a full day of recording and editing can now be done in under an hour.

cards.headline: Text-to-speech: your new voiceover engine
cards.body: Modern AI voices are indistinguishable from human speech. Whether you need a narration for a course, a voiceover for a video, or an audio version of your blog, text-to-speech tools deliver in minutes.
